pull_request_body: A devops command run from a deleted working directory crashed with an unhandled FileNotFoundError traceback from the telemetry setup. The telemetry tracer calls _resolve_git_dir, which calls Path.cwd(). When the directory no longer exists, Path.cwd() raises FileNotFoundError and the command does not complete. This change wraps the Path.cwd() call in _resolve_git_dir with a try/except OSError guard. On failure, the function returns None, which is the same value it returns when no .git entry is found. The caller _detect_vcs_metadata already handles None by returning an empty dict, so the command proceeds without telemetry VCS attributes. The fix is one try/except block of about 4 lines in src/devops_cli/telemetry/tracer.py, plus a test that patches Path.cwd to raise FileNotFoundError and a
why: #2531 reports that a devops command run from a deleted working directory prints a FileNotFoundError traceback from _resolve_git_dir in the telemetry setup. The command does not report a clean error and does not complete. The root cause is that Path.cwd() raises FileNotFoundError when the directory no longer exists, and _resolve_git_dir does not catch it.
what_changes: Wrap the Path.cwd() call in _resolve_git_dir with a try/except OSError guard that returns None on failure.
Add a test that patches Path.cwd to raise FileNotFoundError and asserts _resolve_git_dir returns None.
Add a test that confirms _resolve_git_dir still returns the correct .git path for a valid working directory.
feasibility: The code at src/devops_cli/telemetry/tracer.py line 628 shows current = (start_dir or Path.cwd()).resolve() with no exception handling around Path.cwd(). This confirms the premise of the issue.
The same file already catches OSError in _resolve_git_dir_from_file (line 618) and _read_packed_refs (line 596), so catching OSError is the established pattern in this module.
The caller _detect_vcs_metadata (line 646) already handles a None return from _resolve_git_dir by returning an empty dict, so returning None on a deleted CWD is consistent with the existing contract.
First check: run uv run devops ci test tests/test_tracer.py to confirm the new test passes and existing tests are unaffected.
Second check: run uv run devops ci test to confirm the full test suite passes with the guard in place.
existing_tool: No external tool or library covers this need. The fix is a try/except OSError block of about 4 lines around the Path.cwd() call in _resolve_git_dir (src/devops_cli/telemetry/tracer.py:628). The written cost is one guard block, one test case, and the maintenance of that guard for the lifetime of the function. No internal code is deleted.

decisions.decision: Catch OSError in _resolve_git_dir at the Path.cwd() call site
decisions.reason: This is the origin of the exception. The function already returns None when no git directory is found, so returning None on a deleted CWD is consistent with its contract. Catching it here protects all callers, not just _detect_vcs_metadata.

FileNotFoundError is a subclass of OSError. Path.cwd() can raise OSError for reasons other than a missing directory, such as a permission error on the getcwd syscall. The existing code in this file already catches OSError in _resolve_git_dir_from_file and _read_packed_refs, so OSError is the established pattern.

decisions.decision: Return None when the CWD is unavailable
decisions.reason: The function signature is Path | None, and it already returns None when no .git entry is found. A deleted CWD is another case of no git directory found. The caller _detect_vcs_metadata already handles None by returning an empty dict.

rejected.evidence: This leaves _resolve_git_dir vulnerable for any other caller. The exception would still propagate if any other code calls _resolve_git_dir directly. The fix at the origin is more targeted.

rejected.alternative: Catch the exception in the CLI entry point
rejected.evidence: Too broad. It hides the specific cause and makes the telemetry path less testable in isolation. A targeted guard at the call site is simpler and more precise.
Narrower than needed. A permission error on getcwd would still crash the command. OSError covers all OS-level failures from the getcwd syscall.

rejected.alternative: Raise a custom exception for a deleted CWD
rejected.evidence: Adds a new exception type for a case that is semantically identical to no git directory found. The existing None-return contract already covers this. Unnecessary complexity.

added.name: Deleted CWD returns no git directory
added.text: _resolve_git_dir SHALL return None when Path.cwd() raises OSError because the working directory no longer exists.

scenarios.name: CWD deleted before call
scenarios.when: Path.cwd() raises FileNotFoundError because the process working directory was removed
scenarios.then: _resolve_git_dir returns None and no exception propagates to the caller

added.name: Command completes without traceback from deleted CWD
added.text: A devops command run from a deleted working directory SHALL complete without an unhandled FileNotFoundError traceback from the telemetry setup.

scenarios.name: gh api from deleted directory
scenarios.when: a devops gh api command runs after its working directory has been deleted
scenarios.then: the command exits with a clean result or a single error line, not a traceback

added.name: Normal resolution unaffected
added.text: _resolve_git_dir SHALL return the correct git directory when the working directory exists and contains a .git entry.

scenarios.name: CWD inside a git repository
scenarios.when: the process working directory exists and is inside a git repository
scenarios.then: _resolve_git_dir returns the path to the .git directory

groups.title: Guard Path.cwd in _resolve_git_dir
groups.test: Write a test that patches Path.cwd to raise FileNotFoundError, calls _resolve_git_dir(), and asserts it returns None with no exception. Write a second test that calls _resolve_git_dir with a valid start_dir containing a .git directory and asserts it returns that path
groups.implementation: In _resolve_git_dir, replace current = (start_dir or Path.cwd()).resolve() with a try/except OSError block. When start_dir is None, attempt Path.cwd() inside the try block. On OSError, return None. When start_dir is provided, use it directly. The existing directory traversal logic remains unchanged
groups.verify: uv run devops ci test tests/test_tracer.py
